headline: Crystal Palace sack Pierre Sage after five months with the club bottom of the league
facts: Palace dismissed head coach Pierre Sage on 12 November 2026, about five months into the job.
Palace had lost four league games in a row and sat bottom of the Premier League with seven points.
Under Sage the club won two league games from ten and one of four Europa League matches.
background: Sage was hired in June 2026 on a three-year deal. Chairman Steve Parish said new squad cost rules forced Palace to sell players, and the club had the lowest net spend in the league last summer.
footage_terms: Pierre Sage press conference Crystal Palace

headline: Thomas Frank appointed Crystal Palace manager on a deal to June 2029
facts: Palace announced Frank as manager on 16 November 2026 on a contract running until June 2029.
His most recent job was Tottenham Hotspur.
Chairman Steve Parish pointed to Frank's record of building winning teams and improving players.
background: Frank managed Brentford before Tottenham and won promotion to the Premier League with them in 2020/21.

headline: Frank jokes he may tell more about his Spurs spell and wants no repeat of the Arsenal coffee cup
facts: In January, Frank was photographed as Spurs manager drinking from a cup with the Arsenal logo, before a loss to Bournemouth.
He says he did not notice the cup and called the idea of knowingly drinking from a rival's cup ridiculous.
At his Palace unveiling he hinted he may say more one day about his Spurs spell; Spurs sacked him in February after just under eight months.
background: Frank earned a Manager of the Year nomination at Brentford, where he was seen as a calm, stabilising manager, before his short and difficult spell at Tottenham.

headline: Frank brings three coaches with him to Palace, two from his Brentford days
facts: Justin Cochrane joins as first-team coach; he worked with Frank at Brentford and Tottenham and currently works with England.
Chris Haslam joins as fitness and athletic performance coach after working with Frank at Brentford.
Bernardo Cueva joins from Chelsea, where he was set-piece coach, and also worked with Frank at Brentford.
background: Frank is already supported at Palace by coaches Paddy McCarthy and Andy Quy. Set pieces and defensive transitions are named by Frank as key areas to fix.
footage_terms: Chelsea set piece coach Bernardo Cueva

headline: Liverpool beat Palace 3-1 at Selhurst Park as pressure on Sage grows
facts: Liverpool won 3-1 at Selhurst Park on 8 November 2026.
Alexis Mac Allister, Florian Wirtz and Alexander Isak scored for Liverpool.
Eddie Nketiah pulled one back with a stoppage-time penalty after a foul by Milos Kerkez.
background: Palace were bottom of the table, and Sage had lost seven of his first ten league games in charge.

headline: Australia coach Tony Popovic waves off links to the Palace job
facts: Popovic, 53, called the Palace links speculation and gave no guarantee about staying beyond his Australia contract, which ends in March.
He confirmed talks with Football Australia about an extension have started.
Thomas Frank, Sean Dyche and Vitor Pereira were also linked with Palace at the time.
background: Popovic played for Crystal Palace for five years, including their 2004-05 Premier League season, and later worked there as an assistant.

headline: Brighton beat 10-man Brentford 2-0 to jump above Man City into second
facts: Brighton won 2-0 at the Amex on 8 November 2026: Diego Gomez scored in the 15th minute and Pascal Gross added a penalty just before half-time.
Igor Thiago was sent off in the 23rd minute after a VAR review for catching Chema Andres.
Brighton moved above Manchester City into second place, five points behind leaders Arsenal.
background: Brighton are coached by Fabian Hurzeler, and Brentford by Keith Andrews, who took over after Thomas Frank left for Tottenham in 2025.

headline: Thiago red card appeal fails: Brentford striker banned for three games
facts: Brentford's appeal against Thiago's red card against Brighton was rejected on 10 November 2026.
The ban is three Premier League games, covering Everton, Manchester United and Arsenal.
Andrews says the squad is built to cope without key players, and Callum Wilson is expected to lead the attack.
background: Thiago joined from Club Brugge in 2024 for a club-record 30 million pounds and was last season's Golden Boot runner-up. He scored a hat-trick in Brentford's 4-2 win at Everton last season.

headline: Hurzeler says he is fully committed to Brighton after Man United rumours
facts: Hurzeler told a press conference he is fully committed to Brighton and called outside interest speculation.
Reports said Manchester United had considered him to replace the sacked Michael Carrick; Mauricio Pochettino was appointed United's head coach instead.
Brighton are second in the Premier League and face Hull on Sunday.
background: Hurzeler credited chairman Tony Bloom for backing him; Brighton under him have climbed to the top of the table race.

headline: Man City 0-1 Brighton: Ayari goal stuns the Etihad and cuts the gap to the top
facts: Brighton won 1-0 at the Etihad on 31 October 2026 through an early goal by Yasin Ayari.
The win left Brighton within two points of Manchester City at the top of the league.
It was City's second straight league defeat after seven unbeaten games; goalkeeper Bart Verbruggen kept them out.
background: Brighton's rise this season has led ESPN to ask whether they are among the Premier League's most complete teams.

headline: Barcelona renew interest in Brighton's Vuskovic as Real Madrid watch Chema
facts: Reports say Barcelona have renewed efforts to sign centre-back Luka Vuskovic; Bayern, Real Madrid and Liverpool are also watching him.
Real Madrid are reported to be monitoring midfielder Chema Andres as a possible return.
Brighton themselves are among clubs reported to be tracking Club Brugge winger Carlos Forbs and Monza striker Gustavo Varela.
background: Vuskovic was bought by Brighton from Tottenham for a reported 46 million pounds in the summer.

headline: Jack Grealish apologises publicly after returning from a club discipline breach
facts: Grealish had not played for Everton since 17 October and missed four matches after what the club called a breach of club discipline.
He apologised on Instagram to fans and the club, saying he could not help the team in recent weeks.
He returned in a closed-door friendly against Derby at Hill Dickinson Stadium.
background: Grealish spent the first half of 2025-26 on loan at Everton, where injury cut his spell short, and returned on another temporary deal on deadline day. Details of the breach have not been made public.

headline: Everton 3-1 Coventry: Barry double lifts Toffees to fifth as Lampard rages at the referee
facts: Everton came from behind to win 3-1 at Hill Dickinson Stadium on 6 November 2026; Thierno Barry scored twice and Kiernan Dewsbury-Hall added the third.
The win lifted Everton to fifth with 16 points from 10 games; Coventry stayed in the relegation zone on nine.
Coventry manager Frank Lampard complained about three decisions, including a Tarkowski hair-pull on Caleb Yirenkyi that was not penalised and a handball check on Barry's second goal.
background: Everton finished 13th last season under David Moyes, who returned to the club in January 2025.
footage_terms: Lampard referee Coventry Everton press conference

headline: Newcastle 0-1 Everton: Barry wins it for Moyes' side in a second win over the Magpies in four days
facts: Everton won 1-0 at St James' Park on 2 November 2026 through Thierno Barry's fourth league goal of the season.
It followed a 3-1 Everton win over Newcastle in the Carabao Cup four days earlier.
It was Everton's first away league win of the season; Newcastle's Jacob Ramsey was sent off late and Newcastle sit 13th.
background: Newcastle are managed by Matthias Jaissle, whose side admitted afterwards they must improve.

headline: Moyes set to pass Harry Catterick's Everton games record at Brentford
facts: Brentford away on Monday 23 November will be Moyes' 593rd match as Everton manager, passing Harry Catterick on the club's all-time list.
Captain James Tarkowski and former midfielder Leon Osman presented Moyes with a signed commemorative frame.
Osman said he doubts the record will ever be beaten.
background: Moyes first managed Everton from 2002 to 2013 and returned in January 2025, when the club were 16th.
footage_terms: David Moyes Everton record press conference

headline: Man United reportedly weigh Everton's Branthwaite and Fulham's Bassey and Robinson
facts: ESPN's rumour roundup, citing Sky Sports, says United are considering Everton's Jarrad Branthwaite and Fulham's Calvin Bassey to strengthen their defence.
United are also reportedly monitoring Fulham left-back Antonee Robinson, who worked with Pochettino with the USMNT.
These are transfer rumours, not confirmed approaches.
background: Pochettino was appointed Manchester United head coach in November 2026 after Michael Carrick was sacked.

headline: Everton the Premier League's sleeping giant: sixth, but Barry leads the league in missed big chances
facts: Everton are sixth, two points off the top four after 10 games, and are into the Carabao Cup quarter-finals.
They have lost only twice, to Chelsea at home and Arsenal away.
Thierno Barry has six league goals but has also missed more big chances than any other Premier League player this season.
background: Moyes returned in January 2025 when Everton were 16th and finished 13th; he says a striker and a right-back are January priorities.

headline: Brentford without Hickey and Collins for weeks as both are hurt on international duty
facts: Aaron Hickey has a hamstring injury and Nathan Collins a knee injury, both picked up on international duty.
Head coach Keith Andrews says both will be out for a number of weeks, with Collins about two weeks.
Brentford host Everton on Monday 23 November at 8pm GMT; Thiago is suspended and Rico Henry and Kaye Furo remain out.
background: Hickey plays for Scotland, and Collins captained Brentford in the Carabao Cup tie at Sunderland.

headline: Brentford call police over rugby ball thrown at pitch in Liverpool defeat
facts: Footage showed a person apparently kicking a rugby ball toward the pitch from a nearby rooftop during Brentford v Liverpool on 17 October 2026.
Brentford called the behaviour dangerous, referred it to police and are supporting the investigation.
Liverpool won 2-1 with a late Alexander Isak goal while Brentford were down to nine men.
background: The Liverpool win moved Liverpool above Brentford into fifth place.

headline: Brentford 2-0 Nottingham Forest ends winless run and adds pressure on Glasner
facts: Brentford won 2-0 on 31 October 2026: Nikola Milenkovic scored an own goal in the 30th minute and Igor Thiago added a second in the 76th.
It ended a four-match winless run and was Brentford's 100th Premier League match at the Gtech.
Forest had 12 shots but only two on target and have scored just six league goals this season.
background: Oliver Glasner previously managed Crystal Palace before his move to Forest.

headline: Liverpool reportedly eye Brentford's Diouf as doubts grow over Kerkez
facts: Liverpool are reportedly interested in Brentford full-back El Hadji Malick Diouf, 21, a Senegal international.
They want to reinforce the left side in January because of doubts about Milos Kerkez's consistency.
Brentford are said to be reluctant to sell.
background: Diouf is a Senegal international who moved to Brentford in the summer.
footage_terms: El Hadji Malick Diouf Brentford highlights

headline: Alex Iwobi's goal gives Arbeloa's Fulham their first Premier League win, 1-0 over Hull
facts: Fulham beat Hull City 1-0 at Craven Cottage on 17 October 2026 through Alex Iwobi's 33rd-minute goal.
It was Alvaro Arbeloa's first league win after six league games without one, and it lifted Fulham out of the bottom three.
Ryan Sessegnon was sent off late for a foul on Robinio Vaz.
background: Arbeloa is the Spanish former Real Madrid defender now in charge at Fulham.

headline: Iwobi equals Salah's Premier League appearance mark as Fulham win at Coventry
facts: Iwobi made his 328th Premier League appearance in Fulham's 1-0 win at Coventry, level with Mohamed Salah as the African with the second-most appearances.
Kolo Toure leads on 353, so Iwobi is 25 short of equalling him.
Oscar Bobb scored the only goal in the 80th minute, his first Premier League goal for Fulham, in the club's first away win in nine attempts.
background: Iwobi made his Premier League debut for Arsenal in 2015 and rejoined Fulham in 2023. He has passed Shola Ameobi's Nigerian appearance record.
footage_terms: Alex Iwobi Premier League best moments

headline: Zion Suzuki drops a corner as Fulham steal a 1-1 draw at Aston Villa
facts: Aston Villa and Fulham drew 1-1 at Villa Park on 31 October 2026.
Fulham led through a first-half goal.
Zion Suzuki dropped a regulation cross from a corner, which cost Villa a win they were on course for.
background: Fulham are coached by Alvaro Arbeloa and had only just climbed out of the relegation zone in late October after a first away win in nine attempts.

headline: Fulham teenager Josh King called up by Tuchel for England ahead of Palmer and Foden
facts: Thomas Tuchel picked 19-year-old Josh King for England's games against Croatia and Spain, ahead of Cole Palmer and Phil Foden.
King has more goal involvements than any other Fulham player and has played more Premier League minutes than any other teenager in the last two seasons.
Arbeloa says King has everything to become one of the best players in the world.
background: King came through Fulham's academy and has played for England at every level from U15. Arbeloa mostly uses him at No 10.

headline: West Ham sack Nuno Espirito Santo with the club stuck in the Championship
facts: West Ham sacked Nuno on Tuesday 3 November 2026 after a poor start to the Championship season with home defeats piling up.
His last game was a 3-1 home loss to West Bromwich Albion; West Ham sat eighth, four points short of automatic promotion.
Mark Noble, Steve Potts and Gerard Prenderville took temporary charge for the Cardiff match.
background: West Ham were relegated from the Premier League last season while Nuno was manager.

headline: West Ham appoint Scott Parker on a two-and-a-half-year deal
facts: West Ham named Scott Parker head coach in early November 2026 on a two-and-a-half-year contract.
He replaces Nuno, who was dismissed after a 3-1 defeat to West Bromwich Albion.
West Ham were eighth in the Championship at the time.
background: Parker is a former West Ham midfielder who has since managed Fulham, Burnley and Bournemouth.
footage_terms: Scott Parker West Ham player goals

headline: West Ham fight back from 3-0 down at Cardiff in Parker's first game
facts: Cardiff led 3-0 at half-time with Jack Moylan completing a hat-trick.
Divine Mukasa, Arne Engels and Max Kilman scored to make it 3-3.
The draw left West Ham eighth, in the final playoff place.
background: It was Scott Parker's first game as West Ham manager, a day after he was confirmed in the role.
footage_terms: Scott Parker first game West Ham

headline: Parker stays winless as Blackburn beat West Ham 2-1
facts: Blackburn won 2-1 on 7 November 2026 with goals from Andri Gudjohnsen (54') and Dapo Afolayan (71'); Joel Piroe replied for West Ham late on.
It was West Ham's first away defeat of the season and Parker's first match without a win as boss.
West Ham dominated possession but conceded early in the second half.
background: West Ham are chasing an immediate return to the Premier League after last season's relegation.

headline: Referee error costs West Ham: penalty given outside the box in 1-1 draw with QPR
facts: West Ham drew 1-1 with QPR on 9 October 2026 after a first-half penalty was awarded for a foul that replays showed was outside the box.
There is no VAR in the Championship, so the decision stood; Tomas Soucek called it a massive mistake and said the ball was won cleanly.
West Ham missed a late penalty from Jarrod Bowen, and a win would have taken them to the top of the Championship.
background: West Ham were relegated from the Premier League last season and have missed several late penalties this term, including against Charlton and QPR.

headline: Southampton beat West Ham 3-2 at the London Stadium in a Championship six-pointer
facts: Southampton won 3-2 at West Ham on 24 October 2026 after West Ham fell two goals behind.
Nuno blamed a slow start and poor defensive decisions but praised the second-half fightback.
A win would have moved West Ham to the top of the Championship.
background: Southampton started the season on a four-point deduction and ended the day two points behind West Ham.
footage_terms: Nuno hesitant West Ham press conference

headline: Former West Ham striker Dylan Tombides' story is used to educate young players at the U17 World Cup
facts: Tombides' mother Tracy and brother Taylor, with the DT38 Foundation and FIFA Medical, talk to young players about regular self-examination.
They have spoken to around 1,200 players from 48 teams at this year's FIFA U17 World Cup in Doha.
Tombides was diagnosed with testicular cancer at the 2011 U17 World Cup and died in April 2014, aged 20.
background: Tombides was a West Ham striker and an Australian youth international.
